newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia March qtr trading conditions flat-survey.
newsitem.headline: Australia March qtr trading conditions flat-survey.

text.p: Business trading conditions in Australia remained relatively subdued in the March quarter, according to a National Australia Bank (NAB) survey released on Monday.

NAB said after a small improvement in the previous quarter, trading conditions deteriorated slightly. Profitability performance improved slightly, but remained very poor and well short of expectations reported in the previous survey.
However, NAB said business conditions are likely to improve in the next survey, although this may be subject to change given the current activity levels.
NAB said the index of business conditions fell a point to a negative four points in the March quarter, and remained below expectations of nil reported in the previous survey.
"Business confidence has picked up a little for the June quarter, mainly reflecting more optimistic confidence levels in small and medium sized firms," NAB said in the March quarterly.
As has been the case in recent surveys, business conditions are expected to improve in the next quarter, the bank said.
"Given the current activity levels as well as continued destocking intentions and still relatively low levels of forward orders -- this view may again be a little optimistic," it said.
NAB said looking further ahead, respondents continue to anticipate a pickup in business conditions over the next 12 months -- mainly in terms of output and profitability, rather than employment.
